interest: This file is particularly valuable to historians as it provides a comprehensive administrative and chronological register of the diplomatic resolution of perpetual leaseholds in Japan—one of the lingering remnants of extraterritoriality and nineteenth-century unequal treaty regimes. It illuminates the close Anglo-American bilateral coordination led by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and British diplomats to present synchronized proposals to the Japanese Foreign Office, balancing municipal tax exemptions against full Japanese sovereignty. In addition, the docket cross-references significant Japanese legal actions, including Imperial Ordinances governing alien land ownership and immigration, while illustrating how multilateral diplomacy operated as other European powers (France, Switzerland, Italy, the Netherlands, Denmark, and Portugal) followed the Anglo-American settlement model.
overview: This file contains the Department of State's docket List of Papers (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.52 (Lands in Japan), covering sub-numbers 36 through 67 from October 1931 to October 1937, with a list summary sheet dated October 17, 1945. The documents summarized in the register trace extensive multilateral negotiations between the Japanese Imperial Government and Western nations—principally the United States and Great Britain, followed by France, Switzerland, Italy, the Netherlands, Denmark, and Portugal—aimed at terminating the system of perpetual leaseholds held by foreign nationals in former treaty settlement concessions such as Yokohama, Kobe, and Nagasaki. The purports outline debates regarding municipal and income tax liabilities, Japanese imperial ordinances regulating alien property and land-settlement practices, inter-embassy consultations in Tokyo, and the formal exchange of diplomatic notes in March 1937 that arranged the relinquishment of perpetual lease titles in exchange for standard fee-simple ownership.

subfiles.about: Department of State docket List of Papers cataloguing diplomatic communications, consular dispatches, and memoranda concerning land tenure and perpetual leaseholds in Japan from 1931 to 1937.
subfiles.summary: This sub-file consists of seven continuous sheets of the Department of State's Form DS-46 (List of Papers) for decimal file 894.52 (Lands in Japan), covering sub-numbers 36 through 67. The entries catalog dispatches and telegrams between the State Department and U.S. diplomatic officers in Japan—including Ambassadors W. Cameron Forbes and Joseph C. Grew, Chargé Edwin L. Neville, and Consul/Secretary Erle R. Dickover—as well as reports from Kobe and Tokyo consulates and European diplomatic posts. The records detail Anglo-American collaboration, Japanese imperial ordinances, commission hearings, and municipal tax debates concerning foreign-held land in former treaty settlements. The negotiations culminated in draft agreements, Privy Council approval, and the formal exchange of diplomatic notes in Tokyo on March 25, 1937, which terminated perpetual leases in favor of standard property rights, followed by parallel agreements with France, Switzerland, Italy, and other powers.
